newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Economics before ideology, Menem tells Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: Economics before ideology, Menem tells Vietnam.

text.p: Argentina's President Carlos Menem wrapped up a two-day visit to communist Vietnam on Tuesday with a pointed message that ideological differences should not stand in the way of economic advancement.
Menem told journalists that his talks with senior Vietnamese officials had focused on the need for cooperation and avoided confrontational issues such as human rights.

But in apparent reference to the wide gap between the political systems in Hanoi and Buenos Aires he said nations seeking to participate in the international community could not turn their backs on the outside world.
"In this world of a global economy there is no point in being isolated economically and politically," he said, speaking through an interpreter.
Menem's trip to Vietnam, the first stop on a three-state tour of southeast Asia, was the first by a South American leader.
"Economics and politics should be in line with each other, over and above any questions of ideological principle."
Diplomats said the aim was to explore opportunities for expanding trade and other ties between Argentina and a region containing some of the world's fastest growing economies.

Hanoi launched economic reforms and an open-door policy in the late 1980s, but the merits of those policies are still a subject for occasionally intense internal debate among members of the country's staunchly communist government.

Menem brushed the differences aside and spoke of progress in bilateral relations during his visit, saying he expected to see two-way trade -- currently running at around $10 million per year -- improve as a result of the trip.
On Monday the two countries signed accords on scientific and agricultural cooperation. Menem also attended seminars aimed at exploring opportunities for expanded commerce.
He was due to fly to Thailand later on Tuesday before visiting Singapore later this week.
